1.s: God tells Hosea to marry Gomer, who will be unfaithful, as a picture of Israel’s unfaithfulness. Their children are given names of judgement, but a day will come when they are called “children of the living God”.
1.d: Hosea was told to marry Gomer, a known prostitute, as a picture of Israel’s unfaithfulness and God’s unwavering covenant love [[tbd:008:Hosea, Book of]]. “Sons of the living God” is unique in the Old Testament, and Paul quotes it [[tosn:Hosea 1:10]] [[bible:Romans 9:25-26]].

2.s: God will take away Israel’s gifts, then win her back: “I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her.” “You will call me ‘my husband’.”
2.d: The Valley of Achor was where Israel first disobeyed in the promised land (Joshua 7); God would give them a new start there [[tosn:Hosea 2:14–15]].

3.s: Hosea buys back his wife and waits for her, as God will for Israel, who will return to “David their king” in the last days.
3.d: Hosea loves his wife again as a sign that God will restore Israel [[tosn:Hosea 3:1]]. The Bible does not say why he had to buy her; many think Gomer had become a slave through debt [[tosn:Hosea 3:2]].

4.s: God’s case against Israel: no faithfulness, no kindness, no knowledge of God. “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.”
4.d: God brings a case against Israel: no faithfulness, no kindness, no knowledge of God [[tosn:Hosea 4:1]]. Chapters 4–14 are mostly in the order Hosea gave them, from Jeroboam II to just before 722 BC [[tosn:Hosea 4:1–14.9]].

5.s: Judgement on Israel and Judah; they turn to Assyria for help, but God will be like a lion until they seek his face.
5.d: Hosea condemns leaders who trapped the people in idol worship [[tosn:Hosea 5:1]]. God’s discipline (musar) is meant to correct, not only to punish [[tosn:Hosea 5:2]].

6.s: “Come! Let’s return to Yahweh” But their love is like morning mist. “I desire mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.”
6.d: The leaders call the people to repent and know the Lord [[tosn:Hosea 6:1–3]]. Jesus quotes 6:6, “I desire mercy, and not sacrifice”, in Matthew 9:13 and 12:7 [[bible:Matthew 9:13]] [[bible:Matthew 12:7]].

7.s: Israel is like a half-baked cake and a silly dove flying to Egypt and Assyria.
7.d: God longed to heal Israel, but saw everything they did [[tosn:Hosea 7:1–2]]. The king is not named; many think he was Hoshea, Israel’s last king [[tosn:Hosea 7:3]].

8.s: “They sow the wind, and they will reap the whirlwind.” Israel has made kings and idols without God.
8.d: Through idols and political schemes Israel caused its own downfall: they sow the wind and reap the whirlwind (compare Galatians 6:7) [[tosn:Hosea 8:7]].

9.s: Israel’s festivals will cease in exile. They treat the prophet as a fool.
9.d: Israel would go into exile in Assyria in 722 BC [[tosn:Hosea 9:3]]. “The days of Gibeah” recalls Judges 19–21 [[tosn:Hosea 9:9]].

10.s: Israel is a luxuriant vine whose altars multiplied. “Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap according to kindness… for it is time to seek Yahweh.”
10.d: Survivors would cry to the mountains, “Cover us!” [[tosn:Hosea 10:8]]; Jesus uses the same words on the way to the cross [[bible:Luke 23:30]].

11.s: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.” God taught him to walk, but cannot give him up: “How can I give you up, Ephraim?… I am God, and not man.”
11.d: God adopted Israel as his son when he brought them out of Egypt; Matthew 2:15 applies this verse to Jesus [[tosn:Hosea 11:1]]. God grieves over Israel, yet his final word is mercy [[tosn:Hosea 11:1–11]].

12.s: Jacob wrestled with God and wept; Israel should return and keep kindness and justice.
12.d: Hoshea became Assyria’s vassal and then sought help from Egypt [[tosn:Hosea 12:1]]. Jacob’s name comes from the Hebrew for grasping the heel [[tosn:Hosea 12:3]].

13.s: Israel is condemned for idols: they “kiss the calves.” “Death, where are your plagues? Sheol, where is your destruction?”
13.d: The word for idols is the same as for the golden calf [[tosn:Hosea 13:2]]. Paul quotes 13:14 when he asks, “Death, where is your sting?” [[bible:1 Corinthians 15:55]].

14.s: “Israel, return to Yahweh your God” God promises: “I will heal their waywardness. I will love them freely.” Israel will blossom like the lily.
14.d: God’s healing grace is stronger than human sin [[tosn:Hosea 14:1–9]]. The last verse commends Hosea’s words to the wise of every generation [[tosn:Hosea 14:9]].
